thesis: NOVONIX is a pre-profitability battery-materials company trying to build a Western synthetic-graphite anode supply chain for lithium-ion batteries. The ADR has collapsed from a $38.60 high to roughly $3.10, leaving the equity priced near its $79.9M cash balance. Binding offtake agreements with Panasonic and PowerCo, a conditional $754M U.S. DOE loan for a second facility, and a pivot to industrial-grade graphite production in 2026 create a highly asymmetric, speculative bull case. The main risks are cash burn, dilution, battery-grade qualification delays, and dependence on the DOE loan closing.

drivers: Riverside industrial-grade graphite production ramps in 2026 and validates the process
Conditional $754M DOE loan closes and funds the Enterprise South expansion
Battery-grade anode qualification for Panasonic proceeds on schedule (H2 2027)
U.S. tariffs and trade policy make domestic anode supply more competitive versus Chinese graphite
Additional OEM offtake agreements commit the expanded capacity

base_case.assumptions: Industrial graphite generates modest revenue and validates the process, but battery-grade qualification slips toward 2028 and the company needs a dilutive capital raise to bridge the ramp. The stock re-rates off the 52-week low but remains a speculative, loss-making name.

risks: Cash burn forces a highly dilutive equity raise or distressed financing
Battery-grade qualification fails or Panasonic/PowerCo offtakes are delayed
DOE loan stalls or is withdrawn
Chinese graphite producers undercut pricing and tariffs do not provide enough support
Micro-cap liquidity and volatility lead to a continued de-rating

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings update: cash, Riverside production status, customer qualification progress
Riverside industrial-grade graphite mass production begins
Battery-grade anode material mass production targeted for Panasonic
DOE loan commitment and Enterprise South facility development milestones

key_risks: Funding and cash burn — free cash flow of -$84.5M on revenue of $5.6M implies limited runway without the DOE loan or another capital raise
Dilution risk from a capital raise at distressed prices
Customer concentration and battery-grade qualification with Panasonic and PowerCo
Execution risk on the $754M DOE conditional loan
Chinese graphite cost curve and tariff policy uncertainty
Micro-cap liquidity and extreme volatility (52-week range $3.00–$38.60)
